entries.title: Buffer Preparation for QSI-SELEX Trial II
entries.text: Buffer Preparation for QSI-SELEX Trial II Buffer 20 mM Na+ Phosphate pH 7.4 NaCl Imidazole Additives First Wash 20 mM 77 mM 10 mM 0.1% Tween-20, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT Second Wash 20 mM 77 mM 30 mM 0.1% Tween-20, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT Elution 20 mM 77 mM 300 mM 0.1% Tween-20, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT First Wash Ni bead buffer (100 mL) = 100 uL Tween20, 100 uL MgCl2, 100 uL DTT, 0.45 g NaCl, 0.28 g sodium phosphate, 0.07 g Imidazole Second Wash Ni bead buffer = 100 uL Tween20, 100 uL MgCl2, 100 uL DTT, 0.45 g NaCl, 0.28 g sodium phosphate, 0.2 g Imidazole Ni elution buffer = 100 uL Tween20, 100 uL MgCl2, 100 uL DTT, 0.45 g NaCl, 0.28 g sodium phosphate, 2.04 g Imidazole Analysis of ligN20w100 HTS samples Barcodes for the libraries: ligN20w100 HTS PE0 - c1 ligN20w100 HTS PE1 - c2 ligN20w100 HTS PE2 - c3 ligN20w100 HTS PE3 - c4 QSI-SELEX Trial II Upon rethinking the strategy for this assay, I think I just need to purify the protein-DNA mix with Strep beads instead of Ni beads. Since ultimately the goal is to obtain the DNA bound to the protein, and unbound protein will be washed away in the flow-through when the complex is pulled down with Strep beads, this process might be good enough. Hence new protocol for this assay can be split into the following steps: Per well: 20 uL diluted protein + 30 uL 1.55X SELEX buffer + 25 uL DNA 910 uL of Ni beads dissolved in a total 12.5 mL blocking buffer. Separate beads on magnetic rack and resuspend beads in 10 mL of 1X SELEX buffer. Aliquot 100 uL of the beads to each well. Total 50 ug protein = 109 uL protein to a 25 ng/uL stock in TF dilution buffer = 109 uL protein in total 2000 uL (add 1891 uL TF dilution buffer = diluted ~18-fold) DNA solution = 50 ug DNA at 20 ng/uL = 50 ug in 2500 uL of TE buffer Allow the protein + DNA mix to interact at RT for 30 minutes. Pool the entire mix after the incubation = this gives about 16 mL of solution ⇒ split into 16 low DNA binding tubes of about 1 mL per tube. Streptavidin Mag Sepharose beads ⇒ based on their binding capacity about 200 uL beads are needed for capture of around 50 ug of DNA ⇒ 12.5 uL beads per tube ⇒ round off to about 15 uL beads per tube Streptavidin Pulldown Protocol for Biotinylated 91‑bp DNA–TF Complex Buffer Composition for Binding and Washing Binding/Wash Buffer (maintain DNA–TF interaction): Use a buffer that preserves the 91-bp DNA–TF complex while allowing efficient streptavidin-biotin binding. A suitable composition is ~20 mM HEPES or Tris-HCl (pH 7.4–7.5), 75–80 mM NaCl (or KCl), 0.05–0.1% Nonidet P-40 (NP-40) or Tween-20, 1 mM DTT, and optionally 5–10% glycerol. This moderate salt (~77 mM) is chosen to match the complex’s stability range and prevent dissociation of the 20 kDa TF from DNA ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=in%20the%20MB%20binding%20buffer,Figure%201B) ). Avoid high-salt buffers (e.g. the 0.5 M NaCl often recommended for streptavidin binding) because such conditions can strip the TF off the DNA, drastically reducing pulldown efficiency ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=in%20the%20MB%20binding%20buffer,Figure%201B) ). The small amount of non-ionic detergent helps block nonspecific protein adsorption to beads or tube walls ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Section%204%29,the%20biotinylated%20probe%2C%20WCL%2C%20and) ), and DTT (1 mM) maintains reducing conditions to protect cysteine residues. A modest glycerol content (5–10%) can be included to stabilize the TF’s folded state during binding ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Binding%20Buffer%20C%2020%20mM,NaCl%2C%20and%201%20mM%20EDTA) ) – this is beneficial for small DNA-binding proteins and was used in a successful DNA pull-down protocol (20% glycerol for a DNA–protein complex) without hindering binding ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Binding%20Buffer%20C%2020%20mM,NaCl%2C%20and%201%20mM%20EDTA) ). (Note: Any glycerol introduced will be removed later by buffer exchange.) Magnesium is generally not required for typical protein–DNA binding, but 1–2 mM MgCl₂ can be added if the TF or DNA structure demands it (ensure no EDTA if a metal cofactor like Zn²⁺ is needed for TF binding). Include a protease inhibitor (e.g. 0.5 mM PMSF or cocktail) if working with extracts, though for a purified TF and short incubation, proteolysis is minimal. Preventing biotin interference: Ensure the biotinylated DNA is free of excess biotin or biotinylated primers before the assay. Even trace free biotin will occupy streptavidin binding sites and reduce capture capacity ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Purification%20options%3A%20Free%20biotin%20in,one%20of%20the%20following%20options)). Purify the labeled DNA (e.g. via spin column or PAGE) to remove any unincorporated biotin ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Purification%20options%3A%20Free%20biotin%20in,one%20of%20the%20following%20options)). Equilibrate the streptavidin beads in the binding buffer (wash out the storage buffer containing azide/EDTA) so that the beads and sample share the same buffer conditions. Maintaining consistent pH (~7.4) and ionic strength in all steps (binding and washes) prevents shocks to the DNA–TF complex. Gentle Elution Strategy (Preserving the DNA–TF Complex) To recover the DNA–TF complex intact, a gentle elution is critical – avoid heat, extreme pH, or denaturants that could dissociate or unfold the protein. Instead, use a competitive biotin elution: Elution Buffer: Use the same base buffer as above (pH 7.4, ±75 mM salt, 1 mM DTT, no detergent or minimal 0.01% to avoid foaming) and add excess D-biotin (e.g. 5–10 mM). This free biotin will compete with the biotinylated DNA for streptavidin binding sites, releasing the DNA–TF complex into solution. Keep the salt in the elution buffer at a low or moderate level (you may drop NaCl to ~50 mM if desired) to maximize TF–DNA affinity during elution – the complex is even more stable at lower ionic strength, and low salt won’t significantly weaken the streptavidin-biotin bond on its own. The streptavidin–biotin interaction is extraordinarily strong (resistant to most pH or temperature changes) ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=The%20streptavidin,streptavidin%20in%20a%20gentle%20way)), so simply reducing salt or changing pH is not sufficient for elution. Excess biotin is the key to a gentle release: it gradually displaces the biotinylated DNA from the bead without harming the protein. This method avoids any surfactants or chaotropes that might denature the TF. Elution conditions: Incubate the beads in Elution Buffer at room temperature (20–25 °C) for ~10–15 minutes with gentle mixing. Do not heat – even mild heating can risk destabilizing this small complex, and it isn’t necessary if enough biotin is provided. Competitive elution at room temp is milder than the harsh elutions (boiling SDS or 6 M guanidine) often used to break streptavidin-biotin ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). (Those harsh methods yield higher recovery but would denature or separate the TF ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)), which we must avoid.) It’s known that recovery with free biotin elution may be somewhat lower than with denaturants ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)), so to maximize yield we will perform two sequential elutions (see below) and combine them. Importantly, this approach keeps the TF folded and bound to DNA throughout – no denaturants, no extreme pH shifts (we stay near neutral pH), and no > room-temp heat. Rationale: By out-competing the immobilized biotin, we gently liberate the DNA–TF complex. Streptavidin’s affinity for biotin is extremely high (K_d ~10^(-14)–10^(-15) M), so we flood with a large molar excess of biotin to drive the equilibrium toward dissociation. Some protocols use 2–5 mM biotin at 37 °C for faster elution, but here we prefer ~5 mM at room temperature for a truly gentle treatment. If the biotinylated DNA had been attached via a reversible tag (e.g. desthiobiotin or a cleavable disulfide-biotin linker), elution could be achieved even more easily (desthiobiotin can be eluted with dilute biotin, and disulfide-linked biotin can be cleaved with reducing agent) ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=The%20streptavidin,streptavidin%20in%20a%20gentle%20way)). Assuming standard biotin was used, the described high-biotin wash is the most protein-friendly option. Free biotin and any glycerol will be removed after elution by a spin filter, ensuring compatibility with downstream assays. Step-by-Step Pulldown Procedure 1. Bead Equilibration: Gently resuspend the streptavidin magnetic beads (e.g. Dynabeads or similar; use a volume sufficient to bind all biotin-DNA, typically 20–50 µL of bead slurry per sample). Place the beads on a magnetic rack and discard the storage supernatant. Wash the beads 3× with Binding/Wash Buffer (e.g. add 0.5 mL buffer, invert to mix, separate on magnet, remove supernatant). This equilibrates the beads to the correct salt/pH and removes azide or EDTA from storage. (Perform washes in a low-bind tube to minimize bead and protein sticking. You can pre-block the beads at this stage by including 0.1% BSA in the wash buffer if non-specific binding is a concern.) 2. Binding Reaction (DNA–TF complex formation): If not already done, mix the biotinylated 91-bp dsDNA with the 20 kDa TF in Binding Buffer. For example, dilute your TF and DNA into Buffer so that the final binding mix is ~100–200 µL in the buffer composition described above (ensure ~77 mM salt). You may incubate the DNA and TF together for ~10 minutes prior to adding beads to allow the complex to form in solution (this can be done on ice or at room temperature, depending on what preserves the interaction best – since the complex is stable at 77 mM salt, room temp for a short time is acceptable). If the TF came in a glycerol-containing storage buffer, dilute it at least 1:10 into the Binding Buffer to reduce glycerol to ≤5% during binding. Optionally add 0.1 mg/mL poly(dI·dC) or BSA in this mix to act as a carrier and block non-specific DNA-binding proteins (not usually needed if TF is purified). Ensure no free biotin is in this mixture ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Purification%20options%3A%20Free%20biotin%20in,one%20of%20the%20following%20options)). 3. Capture of Biotin-DNA–TF on Beads: Add the prepared DNA–TF mixture to the equilibrated beads. Gently rotate or nutate the tube at room temperature for ~30–60 minutes. This allows the biotinylated DNA (with bound TF) to attach to the streptavidin on the beads. Room temp incubation promotes efficient binding; the TF–DNA complex remains stable in this buffer during this period. (If instead incubated at 4 °C, you may extend the time to 1–2 hours to achieve similar binding, as kinetics are slower.) After incubation, place the tube on the magnet to separate the beads from the supernatant. Collect the supernatant as the “Unbound” fraction – this contains any DNA or TF that did not bind to the beads. (Save this fraction at 4 °C for analysis; a successful pulldown should find very little TF or biotin-DNA here, but keeping it allows you to check for binding efficiency or protein loss.) 4. Wash Beads (preserve complex): Remove the tube from the magnet and add 200 µL of fresh Binding/Wash Buffer to the beads. Gently resuspend the beads by pipetting up/down or flicking the tube (avoid creating bubbles or foam). Incubate the beads in wash buffer for 5 minutes at room temp (or 4 °C) with occasional gentle mixing. Place on magnet and collect the supernatant as Wash 1. Repeat the wash two more times (Wash 2 and Wash 3), each with 200 µL buffer, 5 min incubation. Use the same buffer conditions for all washes – the ~75 mM salt and presence of NP-40/Tween prevent the TF–DNA complex from dissociating while still removing nonspecific background ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Section%204%29,the%20biotinylated%20probe%2C%20WCL%2C%20and) ). Save all wash fractions (especially Wash 1) to monitor if any TF or DNA is bleeding off – ideally, the washes should contain only trace amounts of the TF (a small amount of unrelated proteins might come off if using an extract). If you observe significant TF in the washes, it may indicate the interaction is marginally stable; in that case you could shorten the wash time or reduce the salt slightly in the buffer. Generally, three gentle washes are sufficient to yield a clean final complex ([Purification or Removal of Biotin and Biotinylated Substances](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/technical-documents/protocol/protein-biology/protein-labeling-and-modification/purification-of-biotin-and-biotinylated-substances?srsltid=AfmBOoqfqIotmAdHZgr9Meet-1zNQu6FSgOnXUsW37DKdOsn_j8lwNet:~:text=conditions%20are%20generally%20required%20for,using%20relatively%20mild%20elution%20conditions)). 5. Gentle Elution – First Eluate: After the last wash, remove all residual wash buffer from the beads (on the magnet). Elute the complex by adding 100 µL of Elution Buffer (Binding Buffer + 5 mM biotin, prepared fresh) to the bead pellet. Mix the beads gently to ensure full contact (pipette up and down a few times without introducing bubbles). Incubate the suspension at room temperature for 10–15 minutes with gentle mixing (e.g. slowly rotating or tapping the tube every few minutes). During this time, free biotin competes with the DNA’s biotin for streptavidin binding sites, releasing the biotinylated DNA along with any bound TF into solution ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). After incubation, place the tube on the magnet until the beads clear. Carefully transfer the supernatant to a new tube – this is Eluate 1, containing the DNA–TF complexes. Keep this eluate on ice. (It contains 5 mM biotin, which is harmless to the complex but will be removed later.) 6. Second Elution (maximize recovery): To retrieve any remaining complex, add another 100 µL of fresh biotin Elution Buffer to the beads and repeat the incubation for an additional 5–10 minutes at room temp. Magnet separate and collect Eluate 2 in a separate tube. You can either combine Eluate 1 and 2 now or keep them separate to analyze the efficiency of the first elution versus second. In practice, most of the complex often comes off in the first elution, but the second can recover an extra ~10–20%. (If desired, a third elution can be done, but usually two are sufficient for >90% yield.) 7. Post-elution Bead Treatment (optional): At this point, the beads still have biotin bound to streptavidin (either free biotin from the elution buffer or any residual biotin-DNA). If you need to verify that all TF has been eluted, you can boil the beads in SDS sample buffer and run SDS-PAGE to check for any remaining TF band. This is purely for analysis – do not combine this with the gentle eluates. (If the protocol worked well, there should be little to no TF left on the beads.) 8. Buffer Exchange and Concentration: The eluates (combined) contain the TF–DNA complexes in a buffer with ~5 mM biotin, ~75 mM salt, and possibly glycerol from earlier steps. To make this sample compatible with downstream applications (which may be sensitive to biotin or glycerol), buffer-exchange the eluate into a clean buffer. Use a 0.5 mL 10 kDa MWCO ultrafiltration spin column (Amicon or similar). Pre-rinse the column with water or buffer, then load the combined eluate and spin according to the manufacturer’s instructions (typically 14,000×g, 5–10 min) to concentrate the sample. The DNA–TF complex (~80 kDa total) will be retained, while free biotin (244 Da), salts, and other small molecules pass through. Add fresh desired buffer (e.g. 20 mM HEPES, 50–100 mM KCl, 1 mM DTT, pH ~7.5) to the concentrate and spin again; repeat this dilution and concentration cycle 3× to effectively remove small contaminants ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). After the final spin, recover the purified DNA–TF complex from the concentrator (typically in 50–100 µL). The sample is now in a gentle, final buffer with no glycerol or free biotin (confirmed by the fact that small molecules are washed out through the filter). 9. Storage/Downstream Use: Keep the complex on ice (for immediate use) or at 4 °C for short-term storage. Because no denaturants were used, the TF should remain bound to the DNA. At this stage, you can assess the fractions: for example, run an SDS-PAGE of the Unbound, Wash 1, and Eluate to see where the TF is. The unbound fraction might contain excess TF that didn’t bind DNA (or excess DNA if DNA was limiting), the wash fractions ideally show no TF (confirming the complex stayed on beads), and the eluate will show the 20 kDa TF band. You may also run an agarose gel or qPCR for the DNA if needed, to verify the 91-bp DNA is predominantly in the eluate. If the eluate shows the TF band and a DNA band (91 bp) by gel, the complex was successfully recovered. Additional Notes and Optimizations Fraction collection: We emphasized saving the Unbound and Wash fractions in steps 3–4 – this is to monitor protein loss. If significant TF is found in the Unbound fraction, it may indicate the beads were saturated or the binding step was too short. In that case, use more beads or incubate slightly longer next time. TF in Wash fractions suggests the complex might be coming off during washes; to fix that, use slightly lower salt or add a stabilizer (e.g. 5% glycerol, or shorten the wash). By analyzing these fractions, you ensure that the protocol is tuned to minimize TF loss at each stage. Yield considerations: Competitive biotin elution is very gentle but may not strip 100% of complexes in one go. That’s why we perform two elutions and use sufficient biotin concentration. Empirically, free biotin elution yields can be ~50–90% of the bound material ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). If you find the recovery consistently low, you can increase biotin to ~10 mM or lengthen the elution time (even up to 30 min or a second round of 15 min). The complexes remain stable during this period as long as the buffer is gentle. Do not exceed room temperature or use any SDS/urea, as those would undermine the whole purpose of keeping the complex intact. Alternative elution strategies: Very low ionic strength alone (e.g. <10 mM salt) does not effectively release biotinylated DNA from streptavidin – the biotin bond is essentially unaffected by such mild changes ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=The%20streptavidin,streptavidin%20in%20a%20gentle%20way)). Similarly, pH changes would need to be extreme (pH >11 or <2) to weaken streptavidin-biotin, which would likely harm the TF and DNA. Therefore, we rely on the biotin competition method. Another gentle method reported for nucleic acids is using room-temperature phenol to extract the complexes from the beads ([Simple and Efficient Room-Temperature Release of Biotinylated ...](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6854530/:~:text=Simple%20and%20Efficient%20Room,from%20streptavidin%20rapidly%20and%20efficiently)), but this is not ideal here as phenol could denature the protein and requires additional extraction steps. Our protocol avoids any organic solvents for simplicity. Monomeric avidin option: If routine recovery of intact complexes is needed, consider using monomeric avidin resin instead of streptavidin. Monomeric avidin binds biotin with lower affinity (K_d ~10^(-7) M), allowing bound molecules to be eluted under mild conditions (e.g. 2 mM biotin in PBS) ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=Augusta%20University)). This avoids the extremely tight binding of streptavidin and makes elutions more efficient without harsh steps. Vendors offer monomeric avidin agarose specifically for reversible biotin capture ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=Augusta%20University)). In the context of a 91-bp DNA and 20 kDa TF, using monomeric avidin could let you skip the high biotin concentrations or lengthy incubations – the complex would elute more readily. The trade-off is slightly lower binding capacity and stability of the resin. For the current protocol, we assumed streptavidin beads (for maximum capture), and thus implemented the high-affinity competition elution. Downstream compatibility: After the final buffer exchange, the sample is free of glycerol and biotin, which could interfere with sensitive downstream applications (e.g. mass spectrometry or single-molecule assays). The TF–DNA complex is now in a clean buffer and can be concentrated as needed. If you plan to use techniques that involve streptavidin again (for example, a streptavidin-based detection), it’s crucial that free biotin is removed – our spin filtration achieves this, as biotin is far below the 10 kDa cutoff. Glycerol, which can inhibit dry-down steps or certain enzymatic reactions, is also removed by the same step. Using a 10 kDa MWCO (rather than 30 kDa) is important here because the 20 kDa TF by itself is small; 10 kDa cutoff retains the TF and the DNA (which is ~60 kDa double-stranded) reliably. Validation: To ensure the DNA–TF complex stayed intact throughout, one can perform an EMSA (electrophoretic mobility shift assay) on the eluate versus the input. The eluate should show the shifted DNA band (indicating TF is still bound). Additionally, Western blotting for the TF in the eluate vs input can confirm it wasn’t degraded or lost. Because all steps were done at gentle conditions (~4–25 °C, no denaturants), the TF should remain active. In fact, similar pull-down protocols for small transcription factors have been used to prepare complexes for functional assays or footprinting directly ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Immobilize%20the%20biotin,to%20DNase%20footprinting%20studies)). By following this protocol, you will selectively isolate the biotinylated 91-bp DNA bound to the 20 kDa TF, with buffers optimized to keep the complex intact. The binding and wash steps use just enough stringency to avoid nonspecific interactions without disrupting the specific DNA–protein binding ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=in%20the%20MB%20binding%20buffer,Figure%201B) ) ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Section%204%29,the%20biotinylated%20probe%2C%20WCL%2C%20and) ). The gentle biotin-based elution preserves the native state of the protein ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)), and collecting all fractions ensures any losses can be tracked and mitigated in future optimizations. The final sample is in a clean buffer suitable for downstream applications, with any glycerol or free biotin removed by ultrafiltration. This strategy, drawn from both vendor guidelines and literature on DNA pull-down assays, is designed for small dsDNA–TF complexes and prioritizes the integrity of the DNA–protein interaction at every step. References: Binding buffer conditions for streptavidin pull-down (high salt vs moderate salt) and their effect on DNA–protein complex recovery ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=in%20the%20MB%20binding%20buffer,Figure%201B) ). Use of mild detergent in buffers to reduce non-specific binding as recommended by manufacturers ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Section%204%29,the%20biotinylated%20probe%2C%20WCL%2C%20and) ). Inclusion of glycerol and DTT in DNA–protein binding buffers to stabilize complexes (as in Tsuji et al., 2023) ( [Optimization of Biotinylated RNA or DNA Pull-Down Assays for Detection of Binding Proteins: Examples of IRP1, IRP2, HuR, AUF1, and Nrf2 - PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9965622/:~:text=Binding%20Buffer%20C%2020%20mM,NaCl%2C%20and%201%20mM%20EDTA) ). Necessity of removing free biotin prior to pull-down to maximize bead binding capacity ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Purification%20options%3A%20Free%20biotin%20in,one%20of%20the%20following%20options)). Strength of the biotin–streptavidin bond and the need for harsh vs. gentle elution methods ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=The%20streptavidin,streptavidin%20in%20a%20gentle%20way)) ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). Efficacy of free biotin competition for gentle elution (trade-offs in yield vs. harsh elution) ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=In%20protein%20work%20we%20sometimes,works%20more%20poorly%20than%20guanidine)). Advantage of monomeric avidin for reversible binding and mild elution of biotinylated targets ([Which is the best method for elution of DNA (biotin tagged) from Streptavidin Magnetic Beads? ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/post/Which-is-the-best-method-for-elution-of-DNA-biotin-tagged-from-Streptavidin-Magnetic-Beads:~:text=Augusta%20University)). Vendor and literature notes on handling of fractions and direct application of complexes in downstream analyses ([Biotinylation Guidelines—Creating Biotinylated DNA Thermo Fisher Scientific - IT](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/product-brand/dynal/streptavidin-coupled-dynabeads/capture-of-biotinylated-targets.html:~:text=Immobilize%20the%20biotin,to%20DNase%20footprinting%20studies)).

Adjust Sample to 350 µL 1. Transfer your 250 µL sample into a fresh low-binding tube. 2. Add 150 µL QSI sample buffer → total = 400 µL. 3. First Diafiltration 1. Load the 400 µL diluted sample into the filter unit. 2. Centrifuge 10 min @ 14,000×g. Keep doing this till the entire sample is taken up. 3. Collect the filtrate together in one single tube. 4. Wash Step 1. Add 400 µL fresh Streptavidin Binding Buffer to the filter unit. 2. Centrifuge 10 min @ 14,000×g. 3. Move the filter to a new collection tube (provided). 2. Invert the unit and spin 5 min @ 1,000×g. 3. Discard the filter—your retentate (~350 µL) is now in the tube. entries.title: Cloning of pHRS-HCC library v1
entries.text: Cloning of pHRS-HCC library v1 Cloning of pHRS-Nh100 library and plating on BioAssay plate: Nh (HCC-M + HCC-PCR) Insert size is actually 158 bp (lower than AT10 library), so 5:1 ratio or higher may be needed. By calculation the insert to be added for 5:1 works out to 4.15 ng, but we are adding higher as per the previous calculations for AT10 for this trial. 6X NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix 10 uL HCC-M (vector) – 50 ng 1.47 uL HCC – 7.8 ng 0.20 uL NF H2O 8.33 uL Incubate at 50°C for 60 minutes. Combine the assembled product and purify via column purification. - Thaw chemically competent cells (NEB DH5a) on ice. - Add 100 pg of the chilled assembled product to 50 uL competent cells. Mix gently by flicking/swirling the tube 4–5 times. Do not vortex. - Place the mixture on ice for 30 minutes. Do not mix. - Heat shock at 42°C for 30 seconds. Do not mix. - Transfer tubes to ice for 2 minutes. - Add 700 µl of room-temperature SOC media to the tube. - Incubate the tube at 37°C for 60 minutes. Shake vigorously (500 rpm) or rotate. - Warm selection plates to 37°C. - Spread entire liquid culture over the BioAssay plate. - Incubate overnight at 37°C. Transform and expand pHRS-MYC355 The pHRS-MYC355 confirmed plasmid was transformed into a single tube of 50 uL competent cells. The transformed product was plated into an LB-AMP plate. Testing compatibility of SELEX with Hia5 enzyme treatment Prepare Hia5 buffer and resuspend DNA ligand in the same. In parallel, resuspend the same amount of DNA in the SELEX buffer. Add spermidine and SAM in the required concentration and then follow up with Hia5 treatment. Purify the treated DNA and treat with DpnI. Run the two DNA samples along with untreated DNA on a 0.5% agarose gel. “We tested the methyltransferase activity of psfHia5 with the in vitro assay using PCR-amplified DNA fragment containing several DpnI sites. As shown in Fig.1a, after methylated by Hia5, the fragments should be digested into several pieces (mainly 502 and 532 bp) by DpnI. Certain amount of psfHia5 was put into a 20 μL reaction containing 500 ng DNA, 0.8 mM SAM (Sadenosylmethionine) and buffer A (15 mM Tris, 1mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 15 mM NaCl, 60 mM KCl, 0.5 mM Spermidine, pH 8.0), and incubated at 37ÅãC for 1 h and 80ÅãC for 10 min on a thermal cycler, then add 1 μL DpnI and 2 μL rCutSmart 10x buffer, incubate again at 37ÅãC for 1 h and 80ÅãC for 10 min. Sometimes we set a reaction of 50 μL and purified the DNA before DpnI digestion, and the results were the same. We used to detect the fragments on 1.5% agarose gel, but it needs at least 1 μg DNA to be loaded to show clear bands. So we now load samples on fragment analyzer which can detect as low as 0.3 ng/μL input DNA. 2 μL of the reaction solution was loaded. As show from the gel image and peak images, 1 μL psfHia5 can completely methylate all the adenine in 500 ng DNA fragments (containing about 50% AT) even after diluted 16 folds, suggesting an activity of at least 8 U/μL. ” Comments: - Suggestions are that 1 uL Hia5 (diluted 16-fold i.e. effectively 0.06 uL of enzyme) is sufficient to methylate all adenine on 500 ng of linear DNA Hia5 buffer: 1 mL 1 M Tris pH 8 15 uL EDTA (0.5 M) 2 uL EGTA (0.5 M) 1 uL NaCl (100 mM) 150 uL KCl (100 mM) 600 uL Spermidine (100X) (1X) 10 uL Prepare stocks of 100 mM for KCl, NaCl KCl - 0.37 g in 50 mL water NaCl - 0.29 g in 50 mL water For spermidine also prepare a 20X stock = 20 uL + 80 uL NF H2O Buffer composition at point of Hia5 addition in SELEX: 4 uL protein + 6 uL 1.55X SELEX buffer + 5 uL DNA Therefore for this buffer mix combine 4 uL TF-dilution buffer, 6 uL 1.55X SELEX buffer and 5 uL NF-water. Resuspend 1 ug DNA in this buffer. Dilute psf-Hia5 (1 uL in total of 15 uL with water) [dil psf-Hia5 - dpH] Titration of Hia5 for the SELEX+FIBER-Seq (500 ng DNA per trial) 1. Hia5 ligand + SELEX buffer + 1 uL dpH + 0.5 uL SAM + 1 uL 20X Spermidine 2. Hia5 ligand + SELEX buffer + 2 uL dpH + 0.5 uL SAM + 1 uL 20X Spermidine 3. Hia5 ligand + SELEX buffer + 3 uL dpH + 0.5 uL SAM + 1 uL 20X Spermidine 4. Hia5 ligand + SELEX buffer + 4 uL dpH + 0.5 uL SAM + 1 uL 20X Spermidine 5. entries.text: Hia5 treatment repeat Prepare Hia5 buffer and resuspend DNA ligand in the same. In parallel, resuspend the same amount of DNA in the SELEX buffer. Add spermidine and SAM in the required concentration and then follow up with Hia5 treatment. Purify the treated DNA and treat with DpnI. Run the two DNA samples along with untreated DNA on a 3% agarose gel. “We tested the methyltransferase activity of psfHia5 with the in vitro assay using PCR-amplified DNA fragment containing several DpnI sites. As shown in Fig.1a, after methylated by Hia5, the fragments should be digested into several pieces (mainly 502 and 532 bp) by DpnI. Certain amount of psfHia5 was put into a 20 μL reaction containing 500 ng DNA, 0.8 mM SAM (Sadenosylmethionine) and buffer A (15 mM Tris, 1mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 15 mM NaCl, 60 mM KCl, 0.5 mM Spermidine, pH 8.0), and incubated at 37ÅãC for 1 h and 80ÅãC for 10 min on a thermal cycler, then add 1 μL DpnI and 2 μL rCutSmart 10x buffer, incubate again at 37ÅãC for 1 h and 80ÅãC for 10 min. Sometimes we set a reaction of 50 μL and purified the DNA before DpnI digestion, and the results were the same. We used to detect the fragments on 1.5% agarose gel, but it needs at least 1 μg DNA to be loaded to show clear bands. So we now load samples on fragment analyzer which can detect as low as 0.3 ng/μL input DNA. 2 μL of the reaction solution was loaded. As show from the gel image and peak images, 1 μL psfHia5 can completely methylate all the adenine in 500 ng DNA fragments (containing about 50% AT) even after diluted 16 folds, suggesting an activity of at least 8 U/μL. ” Comments: - Dilute 2 uL Hia5 to 15 uL with water Hia5 buffer: 1 mL 1 M Tris pH 8 15 uL EDTA (0.5 M) 2 uL EGTA (0.5 M) 1 uL NaCl (100 mM) 150 uL KCl (100 mM) 600 uL Spermidine (100X) (1X) 10 uL Prepare stocks of 100 mM for KCl, NaCl KCl - 0.37 g in 50 mL water NaCl - 0.29 g in 50 mL water For spermidine also prepare a 20X stock = 20 uL + 80 uL NF H2O Buffer composition at point of Hia5 addition in SELEX: 4 uL protein + 6 uL 1.55X SELEX buffer + 5 uL DNA Therefore for this buffer mix combine 4 uL TF-dilution buffer, 6 uL 1.55X SELEX buffer and 5 uL NF-water. entries.text: HCCv1cc clone 5-9 plasmid isolation & digestion check Test current dialysis apparatus with pump 1 tubing reset Final virus collection and filtering using 0.45 um filter Thaw LEDGF KO cell lines 1. HCCv1cc clone 5-9 plasmid isolation & digestion check Plasmids for colonies 5-9 were isolated from the HCCv1cc plate. To check for the right colonies to be sequenced, MluI digestion was performed for all the clones. COMPONENT 50 µl REACTION DNA 500 ng 10X rCutSmart Buffer 2.5 µl (1X) MluI-HF 0.5 µl (10 units) Nuclease-free Water to 25 µl Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes as MluI-HF is Time-Saver qualified. Run the products on a gel to check for which of the plasmids does NOT get digested cleanly by MluI - since these should be the ones with insertion of the HCC oligo library. Lanes 3-7 represent the colonies 5-9 post-digestion. HCC clone library has about 24 oligos that may contain MluI digestion sites. Therefore, the assumption can not be made that the lanes containing a single band are exclusively the empty vector. 3. Final virus collection and filtering using 0.45 um filter Collect the second round of viral supernatant into the same tube as the previous day’s collection. Pass supernatant through 0..45 um filters and collect in new tube. Add 1 volume of concentrator per 4 volumes of the lentivirus. Incubate O/N at 4 degrees with gentle mixing for concentration. NOTE: Virus packaged in this round: - MYC355lv-T1 (35 mL + ~9 mL concentrator) - MYC335lv-T2 (18 mL + 4.5 mL concentrator) 4. Thaw LEDGF KO cell lines The following cell lines were thawed: - GP5d LEDGF KO P4 - HepG2 LEDGF KO P4 - HAP1 P2 - K562 LEDGF KO P4 The K562 LEDGF KO cells were thawed in a plain RPMI medium containing 2 mM glutamine.

entries.text: Transduction of K562 & HAP1 cells with MYC355 T1 & T2 viruses Transform ShhBC ligation products into E.coli Concentrate lentivirus for pHRS-Gcla and pHRS-Hcla 1. Transduction of K562 & HAP1 cells with MYC355 T1 & T2 viruses K562 W1 - 100 uL MYC355-T1 W2 - 200 uL MYC355-T1 W3 - 100 uL MYC355-T2 W4 - 200 uL MYC355-T2 HAP1 W1 - 100 uL MYC355-T1 W2 - 200 uL MYC355-T1 W3 - 100 uL MYC355-T2 W4 - 200 uL MYC355-T2 W1 - 1.890 mL media + 100 uL virus T1 + 10 uL TransDux W2 - 1.790 mL media + 200 uL virus T1 + 10 uL TransDux W3 - 1.890 mL media + 100 uL virus T2 + 10 uL TransDux W4 - 1.790 mL media + 200 uL virus T2 + 10 uL TransDux Mix gently by pipetting and then add the mix for each well to the annotated wells. Label the wells as indicated above for both plates. 2. Transform ShhBC ligation products into E.coli For efficiency, it’s always best to transform 100 pg of DNA into 50 uL of competent cells. For the 5 reactions I have, transform 0.1 ng into 3 tubes each [total 15 tubes]. Dilute all reactions to 0.1 ng/uL stocks and then add 1 uL of these stocks to each competent cell tube. Rest of the transformation protocol stays unchanged. Pool the cultures of each tube together and transfer into a falcon & store O/N. After pooling, each culture type has about 0.3 ng of DNA transformed into the bacteria. This converts to about 0.1 pg/uL. Use 200 uL of this culture to plate on an LB-Amp plate (~20 pg). 3. Totally 8 plates were seeded for transfection for lentiviral packaging while 1 plate was seeded for the expansion of the cells. Media was changed for the GP5d and HepG2 cells. NOTE: GP5d cells may need to be passaged tomorrow while the HepG2 cells are still growing steadily but slowly. For K562 cells that were transduced with the MYC335 viruses, there is no need to do anything today. While for the HAP1 cells that were transduced, due to the nature of the cells they grow pretty fast and the wells are almost 70% confluent at this point. Since it is not recommended to harvest prior to 48 hours (to allow for protein/gene accumulation ) NOTE: In retrospect, 300K cells per well for HAP1 for transduction might be too much and may not be in favour of high MOI. For the HAP1 cells this experiment may need to be repeated with lower cell density while a similar amount of virus can be used. Harvest the two control wells of HAP1 cells and reduce the seeding intensity to 1:100, so that the growth of these cells can be controlled.

entries.text: 1. Sorting of HepG2del cells: Cells were sorted and the preliminary results of the sort can be seen below. Cells are generally stressed after the sort and are being cultured in P/S containing high serum media. Around 12 hours post the sort, the surviving cells in culture don’t really show mCherry reporter expression. This could be because cells are experiencing growth and transcriptional lag due to stress (?). Additionally, based on the preliminary results I see, the sorting strategy needs to be further refined. entries.title: PE PCR for AT10, Nh100 libraries
entries.text: PE PCR for AT10, Nh100 libraries Add 20 uL nuclease-free water to two wells of the barcode plates: Gcla - A1, A2 Hcla - B1, B2 GCD - C1, C2 HCD - D1, D2 GCC - E1, E2 HCC - F1, F2 Nh100 - G1, G2 Use the complete 19 uL here to set up an individual 50 uL reaction for the final PE PCR. Per library (per reaction): KAPA HiFi MM (2X) 25 uL Primer mix 19 uL PE PCR1 10 ng NF H2O Up to 50 uL 95 C 1 min 98 C 15 s 62 C 30 s 72 C 20 s 72 C 2 min 4 C Forever 10 cycles of amplification was performed Pool the two barcodes of each type per condition and perform AmpureXP purification: - Add 100 uL of beads to the pooled PCR products. Mix thoroughly and incubate at RT for 5 mins. - Place tubes on magnetic rack for 5 mins. - Aspirate clear supernatant and discard the same. - Add 200 uL 70% ethanol and incubate with beads for about 30 seconds. Repeat this step once more. - Air dry beads on the magnet for 2-3 mins. - Add 30 uL TE buffer and resuspend beads thoroughly. Incubate at RT for 5 mins. - Place back on magnet for 5 mins to separate the elute. Measure concentration on NanoDrop and also run TapeStation D1000 ScreenTape to check the size of the libraries. Cell culture maintenance HepG2del cultures: - Check how the sorted cells are growing and change media to high serum media if the growth is still retarded - Change media for the other HepG2del cultures - Record images for the post-sorted cells HAP1, GP5d cultures - Check confluence of cultures - If too confluent, harvest → combine each type of cells and then seed at lower density into a single flask per condition

GP5del_MYCT2PB2 Sample preparation: - Trypsinize and harvest the cells and spin them down. - Resuspend cells in 2% paraformaldehyde solution for fixing and keep at RT for 30 mins. - Spin the cells at 500g, 5 mins and wash once with ice-cold PBS. - After wash and spin, resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of FACS Buffer (with BSA) and pass through FACS tube filters. Standardisation of FACS parameters: - FSC-A versus SSC-A to select P1 - overall population of cells with correct size and granularity - FSC-W versus FSC-A to exclude doublets: Only select the cells along a straight line, discard cells with larger width P2. - SSC-W versus SSC_A: Select cells along the line or uniform cluster and mark as P3. - Plot P3 for GFP versus mCherry for only GFP cell screening, and mCherry versus GFP for only mCherry screening. Mark these respective populations as P4.

entries.title: Nucleosome microplate reconstitution trials
entries.text: Nucleosome microplate reconstitution trials A1 A2 A3 B1 B2 Prepare stock of lig147 = 50 ng/uL (8.65 uL in 35 uL TE buffer) Prepare stock of 20kblig = 50 ng/uL (20.34 uL in 31 uL TE buffer) Prepare a working stock of octamer in refolding buffer:glycerol = 100 ng/uL (1.85 uL octamer in 100 uL refolding buffer:glycerol). Make a dilution with a concentration at 10 ng/uL and then Prepare 6 stocks of histone octamer: A1 = 52 ng/uL (2.6 uL in 5 uL refolding buffer:glycerol) A2 = 57 ng/uL (2.9 uL in 5 uL refolding buffer:glycerol) A3 = 63 ng/uL (3.15 uL in 5 uL refolding buffer:glycerol) For B1, which is reconstitution with the 20 kb DNA ligand, the same octamer:DNA ratios are unlikely to work as here we consider the nucleosome repeat lengths (NRL) in vivo to derive the actual number of nucleosomes we might reconstitute on long DNA. On average a nucleosome occurs once ~200 bp in the chromatin i.e. ~5 times across 1 kb of chromatin. When we extrapolate this for the 20 kb DNA, we could expect about 100 nucleosomes across this length. Therefore, an octamer:DNA molar ratio of 100:1 (or greater) would be ideal for reconstitution of nucleosomes on this DNA. To check whether excess octamer causes aggregation instead of ideal reconstitution use another lesser ratio of 50:1 for an experimental comparison. Based on this we would need: B1 = 130 ng octamer B2 = 65 ng octamer B1 = 44 ng/uL (2.2 uL in 5 uL refolding buffer:glycerol) B2 = 22 ng/uL (1.1 uL in 5 uL refolding buffer:glycerol) Dilution Steps: Add DNA to salt (10 uL) + Add octamer (3 uL) → Incubate 30 mins, RT Add 6.5 uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Add 9.5 uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Add 14.5 uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Add 22 uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Add 33 uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Add X uL dilution buffer → Incubate 60 mins, RT Move samples to tubes and store at 4 degrees. entries.title: Flow Cytometry Cytek Analyser Repeat:
entries.text: Flow Cytometry Cytek Analyser Repeat: 1. Type dyes needed and drag them to the selection panel - eGFP, mCherry 2. Add Reference Group and use Unstained as the Negative control for each of the dyes that are being used in the assay: 3. Add new Groups for each set of samples to be run & analysed 4. Add marker names to the samples to identify samples properly 5. Select P1 as the stopping gate which is the FSC vs SSC population. 6. Keep all the fluorophores and plots on the Worksheet as they are 7. Set up FCS and SSC optimal thresholds but do not change any of the fluorophore values. Let all the fluorophores be present in the panels shown below the main FSC v SSC graphs. While running the single colour controls, we can also perform gating by adding a population P2 that represents the positive cells for the specific marker we are looking at. 8. Once all the single colour controls have been run, first run the first type of samples (under a new group) with a few events. Check that the responsible fluorophores are giving some signal. For my experiment, the colours/lasers I am looking for are: eGFP - B1/B2; mCherry - B6 Duplicate the first sample and then proceed to Unmix for the first recorded sample. All Reference controls will be listed there. Then proceed to Live Unmixing. This will create a new sheet where P1 population must be selected and the positive and negative populations to be marked in the single colour controls for each dye. 9. This creates a new Unmixing Worksheet. We can label the dye names on the axes here. Then go to the copy of the sample that was created and recorded more events and then record both the unmixed and regular profiles. The copy process may need to be run separately only for each sample in a group. Samples currently to be run: Reference Group: 1. HAP1 Unstained (A1) 2. HepG2del Unstained (A2) 3. HAP1 GFP control (A3) 4. HepG2del mCherry control (A4) HAP1 Group: 5. HAP1 MYCT1PB (B1) 6. HAP1 MYCT2PB (B2) 7. HAP1 MYCT1PB2 (B3) 8. HAP1 MYCT2PB2 (B4) GP5d Group: 9. GP5d MYCT1PB (C1) 10. GP5d MYCT2PB (C2) 11. GP5d MYCT1PB2 (C3) 12. GP5d MYCT2PB2 (C4) HepG2 Group: 13. HepG2_GclaT1+ (D1) 14. HepG2_GclaT2+ (D2) 15. HepG2_HclaT1+ (D3) 16. HepG2_HclaT2+ (D4) 17. HepG2_GclaT1- (D5) 18. HepG2_GclaT2- (D6) 19. HepG2_HclaT1- (D7) 20. HepG2_HclaT2- (D8) 21. HepG2_GclaT1 (D9) 22. HepG2_GclaT2 (D10) 23. HepG2_HclaT1 (D11) 24. HepG2_HclaT2 (D12) Sample preparation: - Trypsinize and harvest the cells and spin them down. - Resuspend cells in 2% paraformaldehyde solution for fixing and keep at RT for 30 mins. - Spin the cells at 500g, 5 mins and wash once with ice-cold PBS. - After wash and spin, resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL of FACS Buffer (with BSA) and pass through FACS tube filters. Standardisation of FACS parameters: - FSC-A versus SSC-A to select P1 - overall population of cells with correct size and granularity - FSC-W versus FSC-A to exclude doublets: Only select the cells along a straight line, discard cells with larger width P2. - SSC-W versus SSC_A: Select cells along the line or uniform cluster and mark as P3. - Plot P3 for GFP versus mCherry for only GFP cell screening, and mCherry versus GFP for only mCherry screening. Mark these respective populations as P4. MNase digestion & testing of nucleosome recon samples From the titration test that was run yesterday, just 2 units of the enzyme seemed sufficient to degrade the 147 bp DNA ligand completely (in 30 minutes). For today’s run: Dilute 1 uL MNase to 1000 uL of total solution with NF water. 1 uL of this solution has 2 gel units of the enzyme (MNase-dil). Reactions to set up: 1. lig147 (0.5 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] 2. lig147 (0.5 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil 3. A1recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil 4. A2recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil 5. A3recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil 6. lig20K (1.5 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] 7. B1recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] 8. B2recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] Incubate at 37 degrees, 15 mins. Add 1.1 uL EGTA (0.5 M) to stop the reaction. Run the samples on a HS D5000 Screentape with the regular lig147, lig20K ligands as control.

entries.text: 1. Set up dialysis recon for 0.9:1 and 1.1:1 for lig147 2. Run MNase profile for lower time treatment & stain gel (B3, B4 recon) 3. Fragment HAP1 and GP5d_del WT genomic DNA to 20 kb mean fragment sizes 4. Image the sorted Gcla, Hcla, HCD cells for HAP1 5. Design new recombinant protein vectors for GenScript order 6. Run MOODS for gapped MYCMAX motifs on hg38 genome & correlate with MYC binding sites in varied cancers 1. Set up dialysis recon for 0.9:1 and 1.1:1 for lig147 Octamer:DNA ⇒ 0.9:1 (A5recon) Octamer:DNA ⇒ 1.1:1 (A6recon) 3. Fragment HAP1 and GP5d_del WT genomic DNA to 20 kb mean fragment sizes Take 8 ug each of the HAP1 and GP5d_del WT genomic DNA and dilute in TE buffer to a total volume of 150 uL. Pre-warm this at RT. Load both the samples in the gTubes. Screw the cap on. Load the gTubes into the centrifuge and spin for 60 sec at 4800 rpm. Then invert the tube and spin again at 4800 rpm for 60 sec. Place the gTube on the UNLOAD position and collect the sheared sample from the screw cap. Run some of the sample on a 0.8% agarose gel to check for the integrity and shear size of the sample. Upon running the gel: What we see on the gel is that the intact gDNA has a band size much higher than the 20 kb ladder and possibly represents a size ~50 kb which is the average gDNA size obtained with the Monarch gDNA extraction kit. gTube treatment however homogenises both the gDNA samples to 20 kb mean size fragments.

Set up test recon for HAP1, GP5d 20K gDNA with WT octamer (dialysis) 1. Run MNase and gel for A5, A6 dialysis recon experiments NOTE: The yield for these A5, A6 recon experiments seems a bit on the lower side for using ~3 ug of DNA. Dilute 1 uL MNase in 1000 uL NF water (2 units/uL). Each reaction consists of ~50 ng equivalent of DNA. Set up the following reactions: - lig147 (0.25 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] - lig147 (0.25 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil - A5recon (7 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil - A6recon (12 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil Incubate at 37 degrees for 15 mins and then add 1.12 uL 0.5 M EGTA per tube to stop the reaction. Run all samples along with the original non-MNase treated samples on an agarose gel (3%). Stain with SYBR Green. 2. Set up test recon for lig147 with commercial Epicypherhistone octamer (microplate) We use 500 ng of each genomic DNA sample (per well), resuspended in 10 uL TE buffer. Add this solution to wells A7 (37 treatment) and A8 (no 37 treatment). Set up test recon for HAP1, GP5d 20K gDNA with WT octamer (dialysis) Use 3 ug of each DNA: HAP1 [C5] ⇒ 100 uL ⇒ 1.54 nM GP5d [C6] ⇒ 100 uL ⇒ 1.54 nM Octamer molarity acc. to 60:1 ratio ⇒ 93 nM ⇒ Prepare 1.52 ug in 50 uL solution ⇒ 7.6 uL of 200 ng/uL octamer stock + 42.4 uL refolding buffer:glycerol [1.152 M salt] Add this to 100 uL of the DNA + salt mix [1.788 M]

Run MOODS for gapped MYCMAX motifs on hg38 genome & correlate with MYC binding sites in varied cancers 1. Purify A7recon, A8recon and C5recon, C6recon nucleosomes and test for MNase protection Prepare more Nucleosome Exchange Buffer B (10 mL): - 650 uL 4 M KCl - TCEP 100 uL - 1 tablet EDTA free PI - 20 uL MgCl2 - 0.5 mL glycerol The 50KDa MWCO columns are being used now for the nucleosome purification. NOTE: Because the dominant buffer in the dialysis recon (C5, C6) is a low salt buffer rather than the Nucleosome Exchange Buffer B, the actual concentration of these samples post-concentration is likely underestimated. It would be ideal to in future split each of these samples to two columns for the purpose of concentration and estimation. Alternatively, do not concentrate these samples at all and store them as it is at 4 degrees. MNase treatment (A7, A8): - lig147 (0.5 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] + 44.25 uL water [A] - lig147 (0.5 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil + 43.25 uL water [B] - A7recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil + 33.75 uL water [C] - A8recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil + 33.75 uL water [D] Run these samples on a 3% agarose gel: - 100 bp ladder - A - A - B - B - C - C - D - D - A7recon (10 uL) - A8recon (10 uL) MNase treatment (C5, C6): - HAP120K (3 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] + 41.75 uL water [E] - GP5d20K (2 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] + 42.75 uL water [F] - HAP120K (3 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] + 1 uL MNase-dil + 40.75 uL water [G] - GP5d20K (2 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin [CONTROL] + 1 uL MNase-dil + 41.75 uL water [H] - C5recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil + 33.75 uL water [I] - C6recon (10 uL) + 5 uL Buffer + 0.25 uL rAlbumin + 1 uL MNase-dil + 33.75 uL water [J] Run these samples on a 0.5% agarose gel: - 1 kb Plus ladder - E - E - F - F - G - G - H - H - C5recon (10 uL) - C6recon (10 uL) 2. Treat PB-treated GP5d cells and sorted HAP1 cells with Ad-CRE virus PFU/mL of Ad-CRE is 10^7 PFU/uL For ~500K cells at MOI=5, PFU needed = 25 X 10^5 Dilute virus in DMEM ⇒ 5 uL virus + 15 uL DMEM HAP1: Gcla+ (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media Hcla+ (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media HCD+ (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media GP5d: MYCT1-PB (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media MYCT2-PB (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media MYCT1PB2 (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media MYCT2PB2 (2 wells) ⇒ 4 uL polybrene + 2 uL diluted Ad-CRE + 1.994 mL media Use the bare minimum media i.e. 1 mL to cover the the cells. Incubate O/N and change the media to complete media next day ASAP After making the mix, add each mix drop-wise to the wells. All DMEM used here is of the high glucose type. All media here refers to transduction media for that cell type. Transduction media - low serum media: HAP1 Transduction media: 10 mL HI FBS IMDM GP5d Transduction media: DMEM high glucose Make up to 500 mL HI FBS (2%) 10 mL L-Glutamine 5 mL

entries.text: 1. Test previous lig147 ligation product on gel 2. Perform new ligation reaction for lig147 and test on gel 3. Perform PCR for AT10-HCC & repeat HCC-pHRS-HCCgb assembly 4. Finish design of new pETG20A constructs 5. Passage & change media for GP5d, HAP1 cells in culture 6. Seed new HAP1, GP5d cells for mCherry, GFP control lines preparation 2. Perform new ligation reaction for lig147 and test on gel First perform T4 PNK treatment for two lig147 (lig147-MASTER & lig147-ROOT) 2X each DNA up to 300 pmol of 5´ termini (Use 2 ug of DNA per reaction) T4 PNK Reaction Buffer (10X) 5 µl ATP (10 mM) 5 µl [T4 PNK](https://www.neb.com/en-gb/products/m0201-t4-polynucleotide-kinase) 1 µl (10 units) Nuclease-free Water up to 50 µl 2. Incubate at 37°C for 20 minutes. 3. Heat inactivate by incubating at 75°C for 10 minutes. Notes: ATP is not supplied 1X T4 DNA Ligase Buffer contains 1 mM ATP and can be substituted in non-radioactive phosphorylations (T4 Polynucleotide Kinase exhibits 100% activity in this buffer). Purify this DNA and then set up treatment with Blunt TA ligase. 2X (1 set each for lig147-MASTER-PNK & lig147-ROOT-PNK) DNA (PNK-treated) 500 ng Blunt TA ligase mix 10 uL NF H2O Make up volume to 20 uL Incubate all tubes at 25 degrees O/N. The last ligation trial was performed for around 16 hours O/N. Also prepare more lig147 as a source for the next experiments: Take 1 uL of the original oligos and dilute to 10 uL Do this with both lig147-MASTER and lig147-ROOT 10X NCAP_F (10 uM) 15 uL NCAP_R (10 uM) 15 uL 2X KAPA HiFi 250 uL diluted lig147 10 uL NF H2O 210 uL PCR4, SELEX_AMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 55°C 15 s 8X 72°C 30 s 72°C 40 min 4°C HOLD Reduced number of cycles to reduce noise in the product. Pool the products and columns, purify and measure the concentration. Also, check the purity of the product on a high percentage agarose gel. 3. Perform PCR for AT10-HCC & repeat HCC-pHRS-HCCgb assembly Amplification for AT10-HCC oligo pool: Dilute 1 uL of the original AT10 pool into 10 uL with TE buffer. Use 1 uL of this per reaction. 10X 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10 1 uL NF H2O 10 uL enhancer_R 🡪 GP5d_classical_R (for trial) OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 55°C 15 s 10X 72°C 15 s 72°C 1 min 4°C HOLD Pool the products and PCR column purify. Test the product on a gel. For assembly use the following reaction: pHRS-HCC (5X) Per reaction: pHRS-HCC (M) 50 ng HCCAT10-PCR 10 ng 2X NEB HiFi Assembly Mix 10 uL NF H2O Make up volume to 20 uL Incubate at 50 degrees, 1 hour. Transform the product into 5 tubes of NEB competent cells (2 uL of assembly pool per tube). Then, plate the product onto an LB-AMP plate. Pool rest of the culture and then store for further expansion. When the initial product for AT10-HCC PCR is run on a gel, it seems like there is no product of the expected size. In order to fix this, let us proceed with a 2-step dilution PCR. AT10-HCC PCR: 10X 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10 1 uL NF H2O 10 uL OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 60°C 15 s 10X 72°C 15 s 72°C 1 min 4°C HOLD Run 10 uL of this PCR product on a gel to check the product. One confirmed, dilute the PCR product 10-fold and run a 2nd PCR. 8X 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10-PCR1 2.5 uL NF H2O 8.5 uL OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 60°C 15 s 2X 72°C 15 s 72°C 1 min 4°C HOLD Pool the PCR product and purify with PCR column purification.

entries.text: 1. Fix AT10-HCC PCR and perform assembly and transformation of this library 2. Perform transduction of GP5del cells with Hcla, Gcla, GCD, HCD viruses 3. Perform transfection of GP5d cells with TF-ORF mCherry plasmid 4. Finish design of new pETG20A constructs 5. Test lig147 ligation products on an agarose gel 1. Fix AT10-HCC PCR and perform assembly and transformation of this library The previous AT10-HCC PCR1 gave a smudge around 200 bp which is not right. The primers are correct. Set up two reactions: HCC1 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10 1 uL NF H2O 10 uL HCC2 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10 2 uL NF H2O 10 uL OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 58°C 15 s 14X 72°C 15 s 72°C 10 min 4°C HOLD Changes: - Corrected annealing temp = 58 degrees - Increased final elongation = 10 mins Check the products for these two reactions as well as for the previous AT10-HCC-PCR on a 2.5% agarose gel. Upon running the gel with the following samples: - AT10-HCC-PCR (old) - AT10-HCC-1 - AT10-HCC-2 From the gel, clean products can be seen for both AT10-HCC-1 & AT10-HCC-2, however the latter has more DNA. Follow-Up: i. Set up another round of AT10-HCC-2 with 2 tubes HCC2 X 2 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10 2 uL NF H2O 10 uL OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 58°C 15 s 14X 72°C 15 s 72°C 10 min 4°C HOLD ii. Set up PCR 2: HCC2-2 X 10 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL Nhancer142_F (10 uM) 0.75 uL HCC_R (10 uM) 0.75 uL AT10-HCC2 2.5 uL NF H2O 10 uL OLIGOAMP 95°C 3 min 98°C 20 s 58°C 15 s 6X 72°C 15 s 72°C 10 min 4°C HOLD Pool these reaction and purify by column purification. Next set up the assembly reaction: pHRS-HCC (5X) Per reaction: pHRS-HCC (M) 50 ng HCCAT10-PCR 10 ng 2X NEB HiFi Assembly Mix 10 uL NF H2O Make up volume to 20 uL Incubate at 50 degrees for 1 hour. Transform 2 uL of the product into 5 tubes each of the competent cells. 5. Test lig147 ligation products on an agarose gel Load the samples in the following order: 1. 147-PNK-T/A (old) 2. 147-Root-PNK-T/A 3. 147-Mastercopy-PNK-T/A 4. 147-Rootcopy-PNK-T/A As a control also load the original lig147-Root. Ligation was observed for all the new sets of samples but not in the case of 147-PNK-T/A (old) which was potentially column purified and therefore did not retain the long DNA. 2. Perform transduction of GP5del cells with Hcla, Gcla, GCD, HCD viruses Gcla X 2 = 1000 uL virus + 998 uL GP5d1-T media + 2 uL polybrene Hcla X 2 = 1000 uL virus + 998 uL GP5d1-T media + 2 uL polybrene GCD X 2 = 1000 uL virus + 998 uL GP5d1-T media + 2 uL polybrene HCD X 2 = 1000 uL virus + 998 uL GP5d1-T media + 2 uL polybrene GFP X 2 = 200 uL virus + 1798 uL GP5d1-T media + 2 uL polybrene Leave the media O/N on the cells. 3. Perform transfection of GP5d cells with TF-ORF mCherry plasmid Change the media 2 hours prior to the transfection. Each well contains about 250K cells. Hence, we add for 2 wells: Tube 1: 250 uL Opti-MEM + 20 uL P3000 + 6 ug DNA Tube 2: 250 uL Opti-MEM + 15 uL L3000

Set up larger scale ligation of lig147 5. Finish design of new pETG20A constructs 3. Try clean up of super long ligated DNA with 100kDa MWCO columns i. Add 500 uL water to the 100 kDa column and do one spin at 12000 g, 10 mins ii. Add 500 uL TE buffer to the 100 kDa column and do one spin at 12000 g, 10 mins iii. Make up volume of sample to 500 uL withTE buffer and do one spin at 200g, 30 mins iv. Add 500 uL of fresh TE buffer and do a wash at 200g, 30 mins v. Invert the column and do a spin at 200g, 15 mins. The spin at 200g does not result in the liquid coming down from the 100 kDa MWCO columns. Speed was eventually increased to 2500g, 10 mins to clear the flow-through and the wash liquids. Both the FT, Wash did not have any DNA but lot of DNA was seen in the context of the elute - however this DNA was seen to be fragmented with a maximum size around 10-15 kDa. To purify a ligation reaction further with a gDNA cleanup kit: Set up 2 O/N ligation reactions: 2X (lig147-ROOT-PNK) DNA (PNK-treated) 1000 ng Blunt TA ligase mix 10 uL NF H2O Make up volume to 20 uL

entries.text: 1. Pick 5 clones for plasmid isolation for recently transformed pHRS-HCC-v2 2. Change media for transduced GP5d cells 3. Transduce seeded HAP1 cells with Hcla, Gcla, HCD, GCD, GFP viruses 4. Transfect HAP1 cells with TF-mC plasmid for mCherry control cells 5. Test Monarch gDNA extraction for lig147 ligated DNA 6. Finish design of new pETG20A constructs 7. Transform TF-mC plasmid into LB-AMP for expansion 5. Test Monarch gDNA extraction for lig147 ligated DNA i. 15 uL of the ligation reaction for lig147 was taken in two low-bind DNA tubes. ii. 200 uL of tissue lysis buffer was added and mixed very gently with a wide-bore tip iii. 1 uL of Proteinase K was added to the mix and incubated at 56 degrees for 5 mins. A wide-bore tip was swirled around to mix the solution prior to the incubation. iv. Next, we add 400 uL of the gDNA binding buffer and mix by inverting 15-20 times, gently. No pipetting or vortexing. v. Transfer the whole mix to gDNA spin columns. The columns are labeled as g1 and g2. vi. Both tubes are spun at 1000g for 3mins. Second spin without removing FT, for g1 = 5000g, 1 min & g2 = 10000g, 1min vii. Collect and retain the FT (in case further testing is needed) and throw away the collection tubes. Add 500 uL wash buffer to each column. viii. Spin g1 = 5000g, 1 min & g2 = 10000g, 1min. Discard the liquid in collection tube. ix. Spin g1 = 5000g, 1 min & g2 = 10000g, 1min. Discard the liquid in collection tube and the tubes. x. Air dry for ~1 min and add pre-heated gDNA elution buffer (30 uL) to each column. Incubate columns at RT for 2-3 mins. xi. Spin g1 = 5000g, 1 min & g2 = 10000g, 1min with new collection tubes. entries.text: 1. Change media for GP5d & HAP1 cells currently in culture & check on HAP1 sorted cells 2. Purify 1st ligation reactions for lig147 and set up secondary ligation reaction 3. Set up large scale culture for pHRS-HCCv2 4. Pick a colony and set up culture for new mCherry plasmid 5. Prepare new 200-bp ligands with PCR and set up ligation trials 1. Change media for GP5d & HAP1 cells currently in culture & check on HAP1 sorted cells For the sorting it seems like changing to the low serum transduction medium actually decreased the transduction efficiency of the experiments - based on the percentages seen in the cell sorter. Due to time limitations, the GP5d transduced cells could not be analysed/sorted. There is a back up culture of this for expansion, repeated transduction and sorting. 2. Purify 1st ligation reactions for lig147 and set up secondary ligation reaction Use the Qiagen HMW kit for purification of 20 uL each of the 1st ligation products. - Pipet 20 µl Proteinase K into the bottom of a 2 ml sample tube. - Make up 30 uL sample to 200 uL with TE buffer and add this to the proteinase K. - Add 150 µl Buffer AL to the sample. Mix carefully by gentle pipetting. - Incubate at room temperature for 30 min. - Briefly centrifuge the 2 ml microcentrifuge tube to remove drops of liquid from inside the lid. - Add 15 µl MagAttract Suspension G to the sample. - Add 280 µl Buffer MB to sample. place microcentrifuge tube with sample into tube holder. - Place tube holder onto mixer. Incubate at room temperature for 3 min at 1400 rpm. Place the tube holder on the magnetic base, wait until bead separation has been completed (~1 min), and remove the supernatant. - Add 700 µl Buffer MW1 to the sample and place the tube holder onto the mixer. Incubate at room temperature for 1 min at 1400 rpm. Place the tube holder on the magnetic base, wait until bead separation has been completed (~1 min), and remove the supernatant. Repeat the wash again. - Add 700 µl Buffer PE to the sample and place the tube holder onto the mixer. Incubate at room temperature for 1 min at 1400 rpm. Place the tube holder on the magnetic base, wait until bead separation has been completed (~1 min), and remove the supernatant. Repeat the wash again. - Rinse the particles with 700 µl distilled water while the beads are fixed to the walls of the microcentrifuge tube. Incubate for 1 min and remove the supernatant. - Remove the tube holder from the magnetic base and add an appropriate volume of Buffer AE (100–200 µl). Incubate at room temperature for 3 min at 1400 rpm. Place tube holder onto magnetic base, wait until bead separation is completed (~1 min), and transfer supernatant with high-molecular-weight DNA to a new microcentrifuge tube. - Run the samples on a SpeedVac for about 45 mins with no heating. Ligate around 400-500 ng of this purified DNA O/N with: 1. Blunt T/A ligase - reaction volume 25 uL 2. T4 DNA ligase - reaction volume 25 uL 5. Prepare new 200-bp ligands with PCR and set up ligation trials Take 1 uL of the original oligo per PCR reaction. Amplification PCR (CAPAMP1): lig200noRE_F (10 uM) 2.25 uL lig200noRE_R (10 uM) 2.25 uL 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL ssDNA (1 uL of 100 uM oligo) 1 uL NF H2O 7 uL 95 degrees C 3 min 98 C 20 s 56 C 15 s 6X 72 C 30 s 72 C 40 min 4 C HOLD Amplification PCR repeat (CAPAMP2): lig200noRE_F (10 uM) 2.25 uL lig200noRE_R (10 uM) 2.25 uL 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL lig200noRE dsDNA (from 1st PCR reaction) 2.5 uL NF H2O 5.5 uL 95 degrees C 3 min 98 C 20 s 54 C 15 s 2X 72 C 30 s 72 C 40 min 4 C HOLD Amplification PCR (CAPAMP1): lig200HindIII_F (10 uM) 2.25 uL lig200HindIII_R (10 uM) 2.25 uL 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL ssDNA (1 uL of 100 uM oligo) 1 uL NF H2O 7 uL 95 degrees C 3 min 98 C 20 s 56 C 15 s 6X 72 C 30 s 72 C 40 min 4 C HOLD Amplification PCR repeat (CAPAMP2): lig200HindIII_F (10 uM) 2.25 uL lig200HindIII_R (10 uM) 2.25 uL 2X KAPA HiFi 12.5 uL lig200HindIII dsDNA (from 1st PCR reaction) 2.5 uL NF H2O 5.5 uL 95 degrees C 3 min 98 C 20 s 54 C 15 s 2X 72 C 30 s 72 C 40 min 4 C HOLD Steps 1. Set up reaction as follows: COMPONENT 50 µl REACTION DNA 1 µg 10X rCutSmart Buffer 5 µl (1X) HindIII-HF 1.0 µl (20 units)† Nuclease-free Water to 50 µl 2. Incubate at 37°C for 5–15 minutes as HindIII-HF is Time-Saver qualified. 4X each DNA up to 300 pmol of 5´ termini (Use 2 ug of DNA per reaction) T4 PNK Reaction Buffer (10X) 5 µl ATP (10 mM) 5 µl [T4 PNK](https://www.neb.com/en-gb/products/m0201-t4-polynucleotide-kinase) 1 µl (10 units) Nuclease-free Water up to 50 µl 2. Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes. 3. Heat inactivate by incubating at 75°C for 10 minutes. T4 DNA ligase treatment for lig147-PNK Reaction 1: 500-1000 ng of DNA 1 uL T4 DNA ligase buffer 3 uL 50% PEG 1 uL T4 DNA ligase Total volume = 10 uL Reaction 2: 500-1000 ng of DNA 1.5 uL T4 DNA ligase buffer 4.5 uL 50% PEG 1.5 uL T4 DNA ligase Total volume = 15 uL Incubate both reactions at 16 degrees O/N.

Needle shearing for HMW HAP1 DNA Take 87.95 uL of original sample + 62.05 uL TE buffer. Load the gTubes into the centrifuge and spin for 60 sec at 7200 rpm. entries.text: 1. ligN40w107 PCR optimisation Previously these ligands were halted at PCR1, because the product size seen for the DNA was incorrect. This was likely because the wrong b oligo was used i.e. the incorrect oligo from the earliest design for ligN40w107b. This is now being repeated with ligN40w107b-Re. Estimate the concentration of the annealed DNA product = Dilute this DNA 15-fold ⇒ Make up the volume to 900 uL ⇒ Conc = 5 ng/uL Prepare a 100X reaction mix: Reagent Volume (µL) ligN40w107 Ann 100 Phusion Master Mix 1250 NCAP_F (10 µM) 125 NCAP_R (10 uM) 125 Water 900 Total 2500 Split mix into 25 uL per well for two 96-well PCR plates. 98°C 3 min 98°C 10 s 55°C 15 s 8X 72°C 30 s 72°C 40 min 4°C HOLD Pool the PCR product and run 20 uL of sample on a 1% agarose gel. Measure concentration of the PCR1 product. The gel run showed the correct band size but the PCR product here is not as clean and there is a little bit of smearing, but the dominant band is for the correct size. Concentration of PCR1 = 13.2 ng/uL 2. Repeat of ligation for reconstitution Large scale ligation with a mix of DNA i.e. lig147 & ligN40w107 did not yield very optimal sizes of fragments (L10) This will therefore be repeated with the new lig147 pool. First prepare PNK treated DNA. First take 296 uL (~12 ug) of the lig147 PCR2 pool and concentrate this prior to setting up the PNK reaction as below: 5X DNA up to 300 pmol of 5´ termini (Use 2 ug of DNA per reaction) T4 PNK Reaction Buffer (10X) 5 µl ATP (10 mM) 5 µl [T4 PNK](https://www.neb.com/en-gb/products/m0201-t4-polynucleotide-kinase) 1 µl (10 units) Nuclease-free Water up to 50 µl 3. Reconstitution of lig20K with SBP-Octamer + TF pool incubation lig20K (2x) Use 3.89 ug of DNA lig20K (D7) ⇒ 15 uL ⇒ 15 nM [at 2 M salt concentration] Octamer molarity acc. to 60:1 ratio ⇒ 0.9 uM ⇒ 2.11 ug in 5 uL ⇒ Prepare 500 ng/uL stock OSH500 (0.83 uL + 11.17 uL refolding buffer) ⇒ (4.22 uL OHS500 + 0.78 uL refolding buffer + glycerol) [1.84 M] Post-reconstitution, the assembled nucleosomes are to be enriched with SBP beads to enrich only the fragments of DNA with assembled nucleosomes. Based on the actual NCAP-SELEX protocol, when the beads are added to the nucleosomes for purification, the actual salt concentration is ~0.17 M.

For the D8 sample, the column had sunk into the actual buffer exchange tube – these will either lead to total loss or poor recovery of the sample. For this sample: 1. Pre-Rinse Filter 1. Add 500 µL nuclease-free water to the filter (upper chamber). 2. Centrifuge 10 min @ 10,000×g. 3. Discard the filtrate (flow-through). 2. Adjust Sample to 350 µL 1. Transfer 200 µL sample into a fresh low-binding tube. 2. Add 300 µL Nucleosome Buffer C → total = 500 µL. 3. First Diafiltration 1. Load the 500 µL diluted sample into the filter unit. 2. Centrifuge 10 min @ 10,000×g. 3. Discard the filtrate (contains imidazole, Tween, etc.). 4. Wash Step 1. Add 200 µL fresh Streptavidin Binding Buffer to the filter unit. 2. Centrifuge 10 min @ 10,000×g. 3. Discard the filtrate. > If you suspect residual imidazole, repeat this wash (step 4) once more with another 350 µL. 5. Recover Buffer-Exchanged Sample 1. Move the filter to a new collection tube (provided). 2. Invert the unit and spin 5 min @ 1,000×g. 3. Discard the filter—your retentate is now in the tube. entries.title: Cycle 1 NCAP-SELEX (lig147, ligN40w107)
entries.text: Cycle 1 NCAP-SELEX (lig147, ligN40w107) Step 1: Nucleosome recon - 1.8 uL instead of 1.5 uL was added for the octamer per well - 5 uL each of 20 ng/uL ligands was used per well - For all aspirate & dispense steps change the distance to ‘0.2-0.5 from bottom’ - especially to add to SBP beads Step 2: Nucleosome wash - Rinse 3 times with Water (Ch2) - Prime once with Water - Rinse once with Ch1 & Prime with 200 mL of Ch1 - Wash lig147 plate first (6+6+3) - Rinse 3 times with Water (Ch2) - Prime once with Water - Rinse once with Ch1 & Prime with 200 mL of Ch1 - Wash ligN40w107 plate first (6+6+3) Step 3: Biotin Buffer - Shake at 1900 rpm, 1.5 mins for Biotin elution - 10 uL of P22, P24 were collected and pooled for each ligand prior to moving sample for TF incubation Step 4: TF incubation - There is 30 uL of TF per well ⇒ Take 25 uL TF after mixing 5-6 times and then add to Master TF plate ⇒ Add 65 uL TF dilution buffer per well and mix again 5-6 times Step 6: DNA elution - Incubate at 80 C, 15 mins for DNA elution (on a 384-well plate) Step 6: PCR & qPCR qPCR: 1.5 uL DNA to qPCR plate PCR: 4.5 uL DNA to PCR plate with 13.5 uL PCRc2: 2 uL of PCR1 to PCR2 plate (18.5 uL)

Long read sample sequencing summary NCAP-SELEX process & salt concentration summary Experimental step Total volume (µL) Monovalent salt (mM) Key biochemical event 1 5 µL no-salt DNA added to dried 5 µL of 2 M salt 5.0 2000 mM (2.0 M) High-salt starting point for nucleosome reconstitution. 2 + 1.8 µL histone octamer (1 M salt) 6.8 1735 mM Histones fully soluble; nucleosome assembly precursor mix. 3 Serial no-salt additions (5 → 2.5 → 2.5 → 3.5 → 3.5 → 30 → 15 µL) 68.8 1.00 → 0.83 → 0.70 → 0.58 → 0.50 → 0.22 → 0.17 M Stepwise salt gradient drives histone deposition and nucleosome formation. 4 Transfer to streptavidin beads (+ 5 µL bead buffer 0 mM) 73.8 160 mM SBP-nucleosomes captured; physiological ionic strength. 5 Wash with 140 mM KCl + 5 mM NaCl buffer; residual ≈ 5 µL 5.0 145 mM Removes unbound/weak species; retains stable nucleosomes. 6 Add 25 µL biotin + imidazole buffer (70 mM KCl + 2.5 mM NaCl) → mix 2 min 30.0 84.6 mM Biotin displaces SBP-octamers; nucleosomes released into supernatant. 7 Collect 28 µL supernatant + add 4.5 µL His-TF mix (150 mM) 32.5 96.7 mM TF–nucleosome complexes form in solution; moderate, TF-friendly salt. 8 Transfer to Ni beads (+ 5 µL 0 mM buffer) 37.5 83.9 mM His-tagged TFs (± bound nucleosomes) bind Ni; co-capture of complexes. 9 Wash with low-salt Ni buffer (70 mM KCl + 2.5 mM NaCl + 0.5 mM MgCl₂ + 2 mM β-ME); residual ≈ 5 µL 5.0 72.5 mM Removes unbound nucleosomes, free TFs, biotin, imidazole; leaves specific complexes. 10 Add 35 µL elution buffer (0.1 % Tween, 10 mM Tris pH 7.8, 1 mM MgCl₂) + heat 80 °C × 15 min 40.0 ≈ 9 mM Heat breaks His–Ni bonds; proteins denature, nucleosomes dissociate, DNA released.
