entries.title: Expected size for the PE PCR products:
entries.text: Expected size for the PE PCR products: lig147 libraries = 225 bp ligN40w107 libraries = 311 bp Clean-Up of SELEX libraries for AVITI sequencing Briefly: - For each library I take 1 mL of the sample and concentrate this in the SpeedVac for about ~2 hours - Then perform size selection as shown below - Dilute the samples 100-fold and then use 2 uL of each to run on a TapeStation HSD5000 SPRIselect Bead-Based Size Selection Protocol for Retaining 100-400 bp Fragments and Removing >500 bp Fragments (Modified with a 0.75× ratio for better exclusion of larger fragments) This protocol is optimized for SPRIselect beads (Beckman Coulter) to selectively retain 100-400 bp DNA fragments, while removing fragments >500 bp, using a higher bead-to-sample ratio (0.7× instead of 0.6×) to improve exclusion of large fragments. Materials Needed • SPRIselect beads (Beckman Coulter, B23317) • Freshly prepared 80% ethanol (molecular biology grade) • 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0 or nuclease-free water • Magnetic stand for bead separation • Pipettes and tips • DNA sample (e.g., PCR product, fragmented DNA library) • 0.2 mL or 1.5 mL tubes (depending on sample volume) Protocol Overview This protocol consists of a two-step size selection: 1. First selection (high cutoff step) – Removes large fragments (>500 bp). 2. Second selection (low cutoff step) – Retains the desired 100-400 bp range while removing fragments <100 bp. Step-by-Step Protocol Step 1: First Bead Selection to Remove Large Fragments (>500 bp) 1. Resuspend SPRIselect beads by vortexing or pipetting thoroughly. 2. In a clean PCR or 1.5 mL tube, mix your DNA sample with SPRIselect beads at a 0.75× bead-to-sample ratio: • Example: For 50 µL of DNA sample, add 35 µL of SPRIselect beads. 3. Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down or vortexing briefly. 4. Incubate at room temperature for 5-10 minutes to allow binding. 5. Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes, or until the solution clears. 6. Carefully transfer the supernatant (which contains fragments <500 bp) to a new clean tube. Do not disturb the beads, as they contain larger fragments bound to them. 7. Discard the beads containing the >500 bp fragments. Step 2: Second Bead Selection to Remove Small Fragments (<100 bp) 8. Add (1.8x – 0.75x) SPRIselect beads to the collected supernatant: • Example: If you have 50 µL of supernatant, add 55 µL of SPRIselect beads. 9. Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down or vortexing briefly. 10. Incubate at room temperature for 5-10 minutes. 11. Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes, or until the solution clears. 12. Carefully remove and discard the supernatant, which contains unwanted fragments <100 bp. 13. Keeping the tube on the magnetic stand, add 200 µL of freshly prepared 85% ethanol, avoiding bead resuspension. 14. Incubate for 30 seconds, then carefully remove the ethanol. 15. Repeat Steps 13-14 for a second ethanol wash. 16. Air-dry the beads for 2-3 minutes (do not over-dry, as it may reduce DNA recovery). 17. Remove the tube from the magnetic stand and resuspend the beads in 20-50 µL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) or nuclease-free water. 18. Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes. 19. Place the tube back on the magnetic stand for 1-2 minutes. 20. Transfer the clear eluate to a new tube—this contains your size-selected DNA (100-400 bp). Quality Control • Assess DNA fragment size distribution using an Agilent Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, or gel electrophoresis. • Measure DNA concentration using a Qubit fluorometer or Nanodrop spectrophotometer. • Confirm fragment size enrichment before proceeding to downstream applications. Expected Results • Retained DNA fragments: 100-400 bp • Removed fragments: >500 bp (high molecular weight contaminants) and <100 bp (adapter dimers, primer-dimers, or short degradation products) Notes & Optimizations • The 0.7× ratio increases the likelihood of excluding larger fragments (>500 bp) but may slightly reduce yield. • If small fragments persist, increasing the second bead selection ratio may help remove more unwanted <100 bp fragments. • Avoid overdrying the beads during ethanol washes to prevent low DNA recovery. • Ensure beads are fully resuspended before use for consistency.

entries.text: Bradford assay for ELF2 and ELF2 mutant 3 protein estimation Proteins to be measured: ELF2 WT (new) ELF2 WT DBD → from Q3 DBD (Well E4) ELF2 mutant 3 1. Pipette 5 µL of each standard or unknown sample into the appropriate microplate wells (e.g., Thermo Scientific™ Pierce™ 96-Well Plates, Cat. No. 15041). 2. Add 250 µL of the Bradford reagent to each well, then mix with plate shaker for 30 seconds. 3. Remove the plate from the shaker. 4. Incubate the plate for 10 minutes at RT. 5. Measure the absorbance at or near 595 nm with a plate reader. 6. Subtract the average 595 nm measurement for the blank replicates from the 595 nm measurements of all other individual standard and unknown sample replicates. Pierce™ Bradford Protein Assay Kit User Guide 3 7. Prepare a standard curve by plotting the average blank-corrected 595 nm measurement for each BSA standard vs. its concentration in µg/mL. Use the standard curve to determine the protein concentration of each unknown sample. Note: If using curve-fitting algorithms associated with a microplate reader, a four-parameter (quadratic) or best-fit curve will provide more accurate results than a purely linear fit. If plotting results by hand, a point-to-point curve is preferable to a linear fit to the standard points. entries.text: Updates at the beginning of the day 1. In terms of TC, 293T cells were discarded and new media was prepared for GP5d cells. 50K cells/well were seeded for 3 12-well plates Diagnostic EcoRV digestion ELFlig2 and ELFlig3 were digested with EcoRV for 30 mins & 60 mins. Following samples were loaded on a 3% agarose gel for checking: 1. ELFlig2 2. ELFlig3 3. ELFlig2-EcoRV30m 4. ELFlig3-EcoRV30m 5. ELFlig2-EcoRV60m 6. ELFlig3-EcoRV60m 7. ELFlig1nuc Run slowly at 85 V, 60 mins. SELEX checklist 1. Ligand plates lig70N - Prepare 15 X 400 = 6000 uL of stock [Requires 15 X 20 X 400 = 120 ug DNA] lig200 - Prepare 15 X 400 = 6000 uL of stock [Requires 15 X 20 X 400 = 120 ug DNA] For each ligand split into 62.5 uL per well of a 96-well storage plate. From here aliquot evenly (15 uL per well) to NUNC 384-well plates. Store these ligand plates after labelling at -20. 2. Biotin Buffer plates 200 mL 1X TCAPT Block 100 mL Biotin 0.49 g Imidazole 0.68 g 10 M NaOH 120 uL Make up the volume to 200 mL. DO NOT filter and aliquot 25 uL per well to 12 plates (needs ~120 mL buffer). Clean-up ELFlig1 nucleosomes (removal of free DNA population) Pre-Rinse Filter Add 500 µL nuclease-free water to the filter (upper chamber) of a 100 kDa column. Centrifuge 10 min @ 14,000×g. Discard the filtrate (flow-through). Adjust Sample to 200 µL Transfer your 200 µL sample into a fresh low-binding tube. First Diafiltration Load the 200 µL sample into the filter unit. Centrifuge 10 min @ 14,000×g. Store the filtrate (contains imidazole, Tween, etc.) so that it can be checked for any remaining DNA, protein. Incubate at RT for 10 mins. - Place tubes on magnetic rack and allow liquid to separate from beads for 5 mins. - Perform two washes with 80% ethanol (200-300 uL each) - Allow the beads to dry for ~30s and then add fresh TE buffer in 40 uL for elution. Collect separated supernatant as purified DNA sample. - Repeat last two steps with a smaller volume of 10 uL for improved yield.

entries.text: Footprinting of long random DNA from Yujiao Take entire pool of this sample and set up the following reaction: Hia5 buffer Hia5 Sample Two samples: 1. ligYJnuc 2. lig50Knuc Set up two reaction per sample: Component Volume Final condition Complete Hia5 Buffer A 21.25 µL minus sample volume 1× 32 mM SAM 1.25 µL 0.8 mM Hia5 enzyme 2.5 µL Twice your previous enzyme input Nuclei/sample ~25 uL Same or less than original Total 50 µL Salt concentration during the reaction ⇒ 72-78 mM salt Incubate at 37 C, 1.5 hours. Mix thoroughly and incubate at RT for 5 mins. - Place tubes on magnetic rack and allow liquid to separate from beads for 5 mins. Collect separated supernatant as purified DNA sample.

entries.text: Glycerol Stocks for new clones - Prepare LB (with antibiotics) + 50% glycerol → filter sterilised - Take 500 uL culture + 500 uL sterilised glycerol media - Place 150 uL in each well of a 96-well plate (prepare duplicates) KLF1 LHX2 LBX1 WT1 MEF2A NKX2-2 NACC2 NACC1 POGZ POGK IRF1 NFIA NFIL3 TBX6 BEND3 TETRNEW IKZF1 BEND5 BEND6 LHX3 Purification of TdT reactions - To each subpool, add SDS to a final concentration of 0.08% - Then do a 1:1 ampure bead cleanup following the standard ampure cleanup protocol. Because the solution has SDS in it, do not mix vigorously (this will create bubbles). - Elute in 40ul NF warm water - Measure the concentration on the nanodrop using the ssDNA function. Concentration obtained = ~102 ng/uL ssDNA Expected yield for about 50 uL based on the original protocol is ~11 ug. The current total yield is ~4-5 ug so far lower than we typically expect.

entries.title: TdT DNA synthesis
entries.text: TdT DNA synthesis 1. Klenow reaction to convert ssDNA to dsDNA [Set up 2 of these reactions] Incubate reactions at 25C for 30 minutes. DO NOT LEAVE FOR LONGER. klenow has exonuclease activity, which can kick in when polymerization is over (when you leave it too long) Add SDS to 0.08%. 1:1 ampure bead cleanup. elute each pool in 25 uL. Measure concentration with Qubit. Concentration = 2. Mung Bean Nuclease treatment Leave the reaction at 30C for 30 minutes. DO NOT LEAVE LONGER. entries.text: Nucleosome Reconstitution Yujiao’s long random DNA DNA → 4 ug in 25 uL → 24.7 nM Octamer:DNA ratio = 50:1 WT Octamer (5.4 mg/mL) → 1.25 uM → 3.4 ug ⇒ 0.68 ug/uL octamer stock [0.76 uL octamer + 5.24 uL refolding buffer:glycerol] ⇒ Octamer stock salt conc = 1.13 M 1.83 M salt in octamer-DNA mix. - First incubate the dialysis column in cold NF-water to remove any glycerol from the column - Add the 25 uL of octamer-DNA mix to the dialysis column PEG solution Weigh 5 g PEG8000 and dissolve in 10 mL sterile water - heat at 50-60 C because PEG8000 takes a long time to dissolve. Proteinase K + SDS treatment Make up value to 100 uL with TE buffer SDS 10%: 2 µL (final 0.2%) Proteinase K (20 mg/mL): 2 µL (final ~0.4 mg/mL) Incubate at RT, 15-30 mins. - Add 1.5X volume of AmpureXP beads and mix thoroughly. Mix thoroughly and incubate at 37 C for 5 mins. - Place tubes on magnetic rack and allow liquid to separate from beads for 5 mins. entries.title: Yimeng’s paper nucleosome recon protocol:
entries.text: Yimeng’s paper nucleosome recon protocol: - Starts with 628.9 nM of dsDNA (lig147) The dsDNA ligands were assembled onto histone octamers containing streptavidin binding protein (SBP)-tagged H2A proteins by stepwise reduction of salt concentration. Specifically, 300 ng of ligands were mixed with H2A-tagged octamers at a 1:2 molar ratio in 5 µL of 2 M NaCl solution. After 30 min incubation at room temperature, the mixture was diluted by sequential addition of TE buffer (2.5 µL, 2.5 µL, 2.5 µL, 2.5 µL, 2.5 µL, 32.5 µL, and 50 µL) supplemented with 1 mM dithiothreitol and 1× cOmplete™ EDTA-free protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma-Aldrich), with a 1-h incubation after each addition. Yimeng’s protocol → DNA:Octamer Ratio = 2:1 My current protocol uses 149.74 nM DNA (lig147) & ~74 nM octamer → (DNA:Octamer Ratio = 2:1) Fangjie used 190.6 nM DNA (lig147) & ~58.13 nM octamer → (DNA:Octamer Ratio = 3.2:1)
